intro.displayText: The Critter Club wants to remember where every critter lives, without writing each home's name over and over. Your mission: help Fern the deer move into a brand new home!
intro.speechText: The Critter Club wants to remember where every critter lives, without writing each home's name over and over. Your mission is to help Fern the deer move into a brand new home!

recap.displayText: Fern is all moved in! Your new word is foreign key: a column like home_id that points at a row in another table.
recap.speechText: Fern is all moved in! Your new word is foreign key, a column like home id that points at a row in another table.

intro.displayText: Real databases are many tables that point at each other, and foreign keys are what keep those links honest. Without them, you get reviews for games that don't exist and publishers that vanish while their games still name them. You'll add a foreign key to Pixel Pier's new reviews table and see exactly what it refuses.
intro.speechText: Real databases are many tables that point at each other, and foreign keys are what keep those links honest. Without them, you get reviews for games that don't exist, and publishers that vanish while their games still name them. You'll add a foreign key to Pixel Pier's new reviews table, and see exactly what it refuses.

recap.displayText: Your reviews can only point at real games now, and Driftwood left the shop cleanly. The gotcha to remember: a foreign key refuses to delete a parent that still has children, so move or delete the children first. And in SQL Server, remember to index foreign key columns yourself.
recap.speechText: Your reviews can only point at real games now, and Driftwood left the shop cleanly. The gotcha to remember is that a foreign key refuses to delete a parent that still has children, so move or delete the children first. And in sequel server, remember to index foreign key columns yourself.

intro.displayText: The Critter Club is making name badges, and every badge needs the critter's home on it. Your mission: put two tables together with a join!
intro.speechText: The Critter Club is making name badges, and every badge needs the critter's home on it. Your mission is to put two tables together with a join!

recap.displayText: Every badge has the right home now. Your new word is join: putting rows from two tables together, matched up by ON.
recap.speechText: Every badge has the right home now. Your new word is join, putting rows from two tables together, matched up by the on line.

intro.displayText: Foreign keys split data into tables, and joins put it back together. Nearly every report you'll write at work, from a shop catalog to a dashboard, is a join. You'll fix two broken joins in Pixel Pier's reports and write a three-table one.
intro.speechText: Foreign keys split data into tables, and joins put it back together. Nearly every report you'll write at work, from a shop catalog to a dashboard, is a join. You'll fix two broken joins in Pixel Pier's reports, and write a three table one.

recap.displayText: Three reports, all from joined tables. The gotcha to remember: a join on the wrong columns doesn't error, it just returns believable nonsense. Always check that ON pairs a foreign key with the primary key it points at.
recap.speechText: Three reports, all from joined tables. The gotcha to remember is that a join on the wrong columns doesn't give an error, it just returns believable nonsense. Always check that the on condition pairs a foreign key with the primary key it points at.

intro.displayText: The Grove built two new homes, but nobody has moved in yet. Your mission: find the empty homes, even though a plain join can't see them!
intro.speechText: The Grove built two new homes, but nobody has moved in yet. Your mission is to find the empty homes, even though a plain join can't see them!

recap.displayText: You found both empty homes. Your new word is NULL: it means nothing is there at all.
recap.speechText: You found both empty homes. Your new word is null, and it means nothing is there at all.

intro.displayText: Inner joins show the matches, but lots of real questions are about what's missing: customers who never ordered, products nobody reviewed. Left joins answer those. You'll fix two Pixel Pier reports that quietly hide the missing rows, then write one that finds them.
intro.speechText: Inner joins show the matches, but lots of real questions are about what's missing, like customers who never ordered, or products nobody reviewed. Left joins answer those. You'll fix two Pixel Pier reports that quietly hide the missing rows, then write one that finds them.

recap.displayText: Nimbus counts as zero, every game has a five-star count, and you found the games waiting for reviews. The gotcha to remember: a WHERE on the right table runs after a left join and throws the unmatched rows away. Put conditions on the right table in the ON instead.
recap.speechText: Nimbus counts as zero, every game has a five star count, and you found the games waiting for reviews. The gotcha to remember is that a where condition on the right table runs after a left join, and throws the unmatched rows away. Put conditions on the right table in the on part instead.

intro.displayText: The Grove has clubs now, and some critters are in more than one. Your mission: sign Pip up for the Star Gazers and make the club list work!
intro.speechText: The Grove has clubs now, and some critters are in more than one. Your mission is to sign Pip up for the Star Gazers, and make the club list work!

recap.displayText: Pip is a Star Gazer now! Your new word is junction table: a table in the middle that stores which critter is in which club.
recap.speechText: Pip is a Star Gazer now! Your new word is junction table, a table in the middle that stores which critter is in which club.

intro.displayText: Lots of real data is many-to-many: tags on posts, students in classes, players and their wishlists. A junction table is how every relational database stores it. You'll fix a report that counts too much, build Pixel Pier's wishlist table, and find the most wished-for games.
intro.speechText: Lots of real data is many to many, like tags on posts, students in classes, and players and their wishlists. A junction table is how every relational database stores it. You'll fix a report that counts too much, build Pixel Pier's wishlist table, and find the most wished for games.

recap.displayText: Wishlists work, and each pair can only go in once. The gotcha to remember is fan-out: join two many sides at once and the rows multiply, so counts and sums come out too big.
recap.speechText: Wishlists work, and each pair can only go in once. The gotcha to remember is fan out. Join two many sides at once and the rows multiply, so counts and sums come out too big.

intro.displayText: The Star Gazers are moving to Cloud Nest, and the old sign-up sheet has their meeting place written over and over. Your mission: move them in the old sheet and in the new clubs table, and see which is easier!
intro.speechText: The Star Gazers are moving to Cloud Nest, and the old sign up sheet has their meeting place written over and over. Your mission is to move them in the old sheet and in the new clubs table, and see which is easier!

recap.displayText: Three rows in the old sheet, one row in the new table. Your new word is normalizing: tidying tables so each fact lives in one place.
recap.speechText: Three rows in the old sheet, one row in the new table. Your new word is normalizing, which means tidying tables so each fact lives in one place.

intro.displayText: Real data rarely arrives tidy: exports, spreadsheets and old systems hand you one flat table full of repeats. Normalization is how you turn that into tables that can't contradict themselves. You'll find a conflict in Pixel Pier's old order import, clean it, and split it into proper tables.
intro.speechText: Real data rarely arrives tidy. Exports, spreadsheets and old systems hand you one flat table full of repeats. Normalization is how you turn that into tables that can't contradict themselves. You'll find a conflict in Pixel Pier's old order import, clean it, and split it into proper tables.

recap.displayText: Customers, orders and order items, each fact in one place. The gotcha to remember: clean the data before you split it, because one conflicting copy turns into two rows and a unique key refuses it. And not every repeat is redundant: a price at the time of sale is its own fact.
recap.speechText: Customers, orders and order items, each fact in one place. The gotcha to remember is to clean the data before you split it, because one conflicting copy turns into two rows, and a unique key refuses it. And not every repeat is redundant, because a price at the time of sale is its own fact.
